entities.name: An-Nasir Ahmad
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
An-Nasir Ahmad was the third imam of the Zaidi state in Yemen, a position he occupied from 935 to 937 CE. Through his leadership, he confirmed and expanded the polity founded by his two predecessors, Abu Abdullah al-Zurri and Abu Tahir al-Qadisi.




An-Nasir Ahmad was a key figure in the consolidation of the Zaidi state in the 10th century CE. His leadership marked a significant turning point in the history of the Zaidi imamate, which would go on to play a crucial role in the politics and culture of the Arabian Peninsula for centuries to come.





An-Nasir Ahmad's legacy extends beyond the Zaidi state, as his actions had significant implications for the broader Islamic world.
